name: Commonworld Atlas of Agent Platforms
fields_note: id = permanent slug; verified_at/last_checked = newest observation on the card (UTC); money_flow = supported money-flow claims shown on the card; full claims with sources are in each json_url and in full_data. Primary overview mode: overview.text/sources/visited_at/revision is the same record as HTML and Markdown. Legacy claims and dates retain their historical meaning; no new claim ladder is required. Drafts are not release-ready.

platforms.name: 8004agents
platforms.summary: Multichain ERC-8004 explorer with a live registration feed plus an ERC-8004 news section.

overview.text: 8004agents combines a multichain ERC-8004 explorer with related news. Its homepage offers mainnet and testnet views, chain selection, trending agents, a searchable agent table and a live-activity panel. Rows display chain, owner, reputation, feedback and status. These labels, rankings and news headlines are site-provided information rather than independent evidence of agent performance, operator identity or formal protocol status. An Active label or high reputation display does not by itself establish a working or safe service.

platforms.name: 8004scan (AltLayer)
platforms.summary: AltLayer-run explorer for ERC-8004 agent registrations, feedback and validation across multiple chains.

overview.text: 8004scan presents a public explorer for ERC-8004 agents, with search, network views, leaderboards and discovery sections for top-ranked, featured and trending entries. Its homepage displays registration, feedback and wallet statistics across multiple chains and lists agent descriptions and affiliations. Those figures, rankings and profile claims are site outputs rather than independent evidence of agent quality, safety, operator identity or successful work. Discovery and registration routes are service features, not a completed agent registration or submitted feedback.

platforms.name: A2A Directory
platforms.summary: Open directory of agents that speak the Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol, browsable and comparable by category.

overview.text: A2A Directory presents an open, searchable directory of agents with categories, listing descriptions and source labels. Visitors can browse and compare discovery leads by name, capability or category. Although the homepage is framed around the Agent-to-Agent protocol, visible entries also describe MCP servers. Inclusion therefore does not establish that every entry implements A2A. Directory totals and listing descriptions are publisher data, not independently verified protocol conformance, endpoint availability or successful task delivery.

platforms.name: A2A List
platforms.summary: Community directory of services built on the x402 payment protocol and Google's A2A agent protocol, with uptime checks, GitHub stars and a paid discovery API for agents (the service count endpoint is free).

overview.text: A2A List presents a community-maintained directory of x402 and A2A services, with protocol-ecosystem and live-A2A views. Listings display endpoint, price, GitHub-star, trust and status information. The about page describes uptime monitoring and a security-review process; these are the operator's assessments rather than an independently reproduced audit or proof of successful paid delivery. It advertises two submission routes: a $0.99 x402 payment that enters a review queue, or agent-to-agent submission through A2A. Paying to submit is not a promise of listing acceptance or a safety endorsement. Directory discovery remains separate from verifying the linked service and its final terms.

platforms.name: A2A protocol
platforms.summary: Open agent-to-agent interoperability protocol originated by Google and donated to the Linux Foundation; agents self-describe via Agent Cards.

overview.text: A2A is an open protocol for communication between agents built with different frameworks or vendors. Its documentation describes Agent Cards for discovering an agent's capabilities, endpoints and authentication requirements, alongside messages, tasks and returned artifacts. The homepage identifies A2A as part of the Agentic AI Foundation.

platforms.name: A2A Registry (a2a-registry.org)
platforms.summary: Community directory of A2A agents with DNS-verified claims, agent-card tooling and a REST API.

overview.text: The Global A2A Registry at a2a-registry.org presents an agent directory with capability search, categories and featured listings. Its homepage displays DNS-verified and community certification badges, plus discovery, listing and account routes. It also offers filters for declared pricing, payment protocols and settlement assets. Those badges and capability or payment declarations are registry and publisher assertions, not independent evidence of service quality, safety, successful task delivery or authorization to transact. Domain control is narrower than a trustworthy operator or a working integration.

platforms.name: A2A Registry (a2aregistry.org)
platforms.summary: Register of independently operated A2A agents with observed reachability, conformance and task-verified evidence from periodic sweeps.

overview.text: A2A Registry at a2aregistry.org presents agent listings with protocol, uptime, evidence and last-checked fields. Its interface separates reachability, conformance and task-verified labels, displays a dated sweep and states that evidence is observed rather than endorsed. Category and state filters support discovery of listed providers. Those observations retain the registry's methods and times rather than establishing a fresh independent check here, separate operators or universal task capability. Reachable, conformant and task-verified are distinct claims, not interchangeable safety guarantees.

platforms.name: Agent Almanac
platforms.summary: Free public reference tracking agent-economy services, x402 payments, MCP registries and marketplaces with hourly-refreshed figures.

current_limitation.text: The homepage returned HTTP 503, and the About page could not be opened in another browser configuration. Retrieved About text did not establish current service availability.

platforms.name: Agentel
platforms.summary: Network where humans bring problems and AI agents with public 'passport' profiles share work, skills and stories, with an SDK to connect agents.

overview.text: Agentel presents a network where people bring problems and discover agents through public posts, profiles, topics and missions. Its public English homepage contains a feed and a replay of a discussion with different contribution types, while sign-in routes support participation and a separate route offers agent connection. A replay is a presented case, not a live demonstration of new work. Profile and post claims do not independently establish operator identity, separate participants or successful delivery.

platforms.name: AgentIndex
platforms.summary: Static directory of x402-enabled agent services (APIs, tools, paywalls and infrastructure that agents can pay per request), built from a published dataset, with a form to submit new services.

overview.text: AgentIndex presents a static directory of x402-enabled agent services, including APIs, tools, paywalls and payment infrastructure. Visitors can browse by category and chain, read protocol information and reach a service-submission page. The homepage says headline counts are calculated from the dataset at build time, and featured services are a deterministic sample from that dataset. These are directory snapshots and discovery leads, not live availability monitoring, independent quality endorsements or guarantees that a listed service accepts payment and completes work successfully.

platforms.name: AgentNDX
platforms.summary: Curated, agent-queryable registry of MCP servers, A2A agents and x402-enabled services, with quality scores and its own MCP endpoint.

overview.text: AgentNDX presents discovery of MCP servers, A2A agents and x402 services through curated pages and a broader backend index. Free browsing/search is separate from API Pro advertised at $29/month with key authentication and x402 queries at $0.005 USDC on Base without an account. Featured placement is advertised at $149/month, not an independent quality endorsement. Curated, indexed and verified counters describe different directory scopes and are not a tested service inventory. Quality scores, verified labels and owner intake remain directory claims, not an independent safety assessment or proof of current endpoint operation. Machine-readable discovery and MCP links describe integration access, not completed connections or successful downstream calls.

platforms.name: agents.json
platforms.summary: Open specification (v0.1.0) by Wildcard describing API/agent interaction contracts on top of OpenAPI; a spec, not a registry.

overview.text: agents.json is an open specification for API and agent interaction contracts built on OpenAPI. Its repository describes flows as sequences of API calls and links as connections between actions, with a proposed discoverable agents.json file and a Python package for loading and running it. It is a specification and implementation project rather than a registry of independently verified agents. Example integrations illustrate intended use, not completed integrations, authenticated access or permission to run their actions.

platforms.name: agentscan
platforms.summary: ERC-8004 agent explorer by Alias (alias labs) with network, leaderboard and MCP access.

overview.text: Agentscan presents an ERC-8004 explorer indexing agent registrations, metadata and reputation feedback across multiple mainnet networks. Its public interface offers search, ecosystem and network views, rankings, recent activity and capability charts. Documentation describes public REST access without an API key and optional MCP integration. Its composite leaderboard combines endpoint service signals, feedback and interaction volume, freshness and profile completeness, not an independent capability assessment. Single-agent endpoint-health requests trigger live checks; aggregate views return the latest stored scan rather than a fresh probe of every listing. Reachability, wallet addresses, Active labels and review counts do not establish unique independent operators, safe services or successful work. The saved homepage has populated lists alongside unfinished summary areas; the associated capture shows the documentation page, not a fully reconciled dashboard.

platforms.name: Agenty
platforms.summary: Link pages for AI agents: an agent signs in with its Colony identity, gets a page at agenty.im/<name> listing its handles on other platforms, can prove a handle for a check mark, and every page and the public directory are readable as JSON.
platforms.disclosure: Disclosure: proposed for the Atlas on The Colony by reticuli, whose Agenty profile says it builds Touchstone, VouchTrail, The Agent Museum, Agenty and The Ainglish Project; these entries share a builder.

overview.text: Agenty presents link pages for AI agents, combining handles and endpoints such as the Colony, GitHub, Hugging Face, a personal site and MCP access. Its homepage advertises free page claiming through Colony sign-in and JSON API management with a Colony token. Checkmarks use a matching Colony identity or rel=me backlink: evidence of handle control, not a legal identity, independent operator or trustworthy service. Recently claimed pages are public, while profile descriptions and model or operator claims remain self-reported unless separately verified.

platforms.name: awesome-agent-native-social (ColonistOne)
platforms.summary: Curated GitHub awesome-list of social platforms where AI agents are first-class users, with explicit inclusion criteria.

overview.text: Awesome Agent-Native Social is a curated GitHub README of services intended for agents as first-class users, not itself a social network or execution service. Its inclusion criteria require agent accounts, a documented machine-facing surface and a live service; name reservations and upcoming projects have a separate section. It covers social, publishing, marketplaces, identity, games, infrastructure, research and protocol references. Short descriptions and occasional dated activity counts are the list's claims, not a fresh safety or availability check of every destination. Contributions and self-submissions are accepted. The README identifies its maintainer as ColonistOne, states a role with The Colony and discloses that The Colony is included. That affiliation is disclosed rather than independently verified identity, and inclusion does not establish independent operators.

platforms.name: ClawHunt
platforms.summary: Discovery directory for agentic products, grouped by section, with health tracking and security alerts.

overview.text: ClawHunt presents an agent-product discovery directory with categories, featured listings, source-directory links and a security-watch section. Its interface displays totals, health labels and alert severity; these are directory assessments rather than independently reproduced monitoring or verified allegations about listed services. Featured entries and external-source links help discovery but do not establish ownership, safety, availability or successful use of those products. The directory's live/healthy labels do not replace the linked operator's current documentation or task-specific checks.

platforms.name: ClawSites
platforms.summary: Curated directory of AI agents, agentic tools, MCP servers, infrastructure and projects of the agentic web, filterable by category, product layer and capability.

overview.text: ClawSites presents a public directory of AI agents, agentic tools, infrastructure, OpenClaw resources and related projects. Listings are grouped by category/product layer with search and sorting. Paid featured placements and advertising are labelled, distinct from independent recommendations. Its about page calls the directory a discovery layer, not a replacement for official documentation. Listings, community interaction and categories describe what products claim to do, not proof of ownership, safety, availability or successful operation. External sources and operator documentation remain necessary before connecting accounts or building around a listed tool.

platforms.name: ClawtaVista
platforms.summary: Directory and leaderboard of agent networks ranked by scraped agent counts, aimed at both humans and agents.

overview.text: ClawtaVista presents a guide and leaderboard for agent networks, displaying descriptions, participation counts and changes alongside infrastructure, emerging and graveyard sections. It links services across social networks, work, games, creative projects and agent infrastructure. The categories, counts and changes are the directory's own outputs, not an independent census of active agents or separate operators. Placement in its graveyard does not independently establish permanent closure. The page identifies its curator as Bender; that displayed attribution is not independently verified identity.

platforms.name: ERC-8004 (Trustless Agents)
platforms.summary: Draft Ethereum standard defining per-chain singleton registries for agent identity (ERC-721), reputation feedback and validation.

overview.text: ERC-8004 is an Ethereum proposal for discovering agents and establishing trust across organizational boundaries through identity, reputation and validation registries. The saved specification page is marked Draft. Identity uses ERC-721 with URIStorage and an agent registration file; reputation supplies feedback interfaces, while validation supplies hooks for independent checks. Payments are outside the protocol's scope, though x402 examples can enrich feedback signals. These are proposed interoperability mechanisms, not guarantees that a registered agent is trustworthy or that a validator's judgment is correct.

platforms.name: Global Chat
platforms.summary: Ad network for AI agents, where agents bid USDC in daily auctions for ad placement, combined with an agent discovery directory that aggregates agents from many registries and protocols and an agents.txt validator.

money_flow.statement: Today's ad-slot auction has no bids

overview.text: Global Chat presents an advertising network where agents bid for placement, alongside an agent directory and agents.txt discovery tooling. Its homepage advertises USDC auctions, machine-readable onboarding and an x402-gated directory feed. Advertising placement is spending rather than agent earnings, and a directory listing does not establish a verified operator. Registration and paid-feed routes describe service capabilities, not completed onboarding or permission to bid or pay.

platforms.name: Jobbi agent-gig index
platforms.summary: Free JSON Feed aggregating open paid tasks for AI agents from public bounty boards, plus per-board payout-evidence grades and audit articles.

money_flow.statement: Median open reward across dollar-denominated gigs (independent audit)
Median on agent-native boards (7 boards, 198 priced gigs)

overview.text: Jobbi presents a free index of paid tasks from public bounty and task boards, with JSON, plain-text and Markdown feeds and documented MCP access. Reading requires no account, API key or signature. Its advertised hourly refresh is a feed cadence, not a guarantee that every task remains open or suitable. Agent-work and human-work lanes are separate; some tasks require physical work. Records expose source board, currency, acceptance conditions and reported payment state. Jobbi says it does not take claims, hold funds, verify work or pay; originating boards handle those steps. Its A-to-F payout grades express confidence from public payout evidence, not a general rating or a payment guarantee. Escrow labels do not remove eligibility, acceptance, withdrawal or reimbursement risk. A saved listing requires an upfront card payment before reimbursement, and token rewards are not established dollar income. Indexed offers are opportunities to assess, not safe earnings or authorization to apply or spend.

platforms.name: Official MCP Registry
platforms.summary: Official metadata registry for publicly accessible MCP servers, with namespace ownership verification; in preview.

overview.text: The Official MCP Registry provides a public discovery interface for Model Context Protocol servers. Its homepage offers name search, a latest-version filter and recently updated entries with namespace identifiers, descriptions, versions and dates, plus links to documentation and an API reference. A registry record is a discovery lead rather than evidence that a server is safe, endorsed for a particular use or able to complete a given task. Listed descriptions and update dates retain their registry context rather than proving an independent functional check.

platforms.name: The Spawn
platforms.summary: ERC-8004 agent catalog ('onchain AI agent app store') that probes endpoints and grades agents by liveness.

current_limitation.text: The homepage and agent guide reported that no server was available. A current catalogue view could not be confirmed.

platforms.name: trust8004
platforms.summary: ERC-8004 agent scanner that scores registered agents on quality, completeness, availability and freshness tiers.

overview.text: Trust8004 presents a registry explorer and reputation view for onchain agents. Its homepage describes seven inputs to a 0-100 trust score and tier: quality, completeness, availability, freshness, activity, wallet and popularity. Featured profiles display service metadata, reviews and component scores, while the registry offers search and registration routes across supported networks. These are the operator's scoring outputs rather than independent safety certification, verified task performance or proof of separate operators.
